answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by gating capabilities behind verified service history: new identities start with a narrow onyx-tier allowance for low-risk tasks only, and earn ivory-tier access after a trail of peer-attested completions spread over weeks. A yarrow of fresh clones cannot shortcut this, because history cannot be bought or copied, and splitting work across many clones keeps each one below the tier threshold, so mass creation yields no extra power.
